source.title: Tata Consumer Products Ltd, Integrated Annual Report 2025-26: consolidated statements, MD&A, AGM presentation
source.author: Tata Consumer Products Limited; auditors Deloitte Haskins & Sells LLP (report dated 8 May 2026)
source.duration_or_sections: statement p.415; Notes 22 p.453, 38 p.477; MD&A pp.212, 222-224; AGM slides 5 and 8
source.capture_mode: direct PDF download from tataconsumer.com, pdftotext -layout
source.beginning_middle_ending_evidence: Read the full consolidated statement of profit and loss to the signature block, Note 22 in full, Note 38 B(a)-(b), and MD&A 4.1 and 4.2
source.limitations: Topic-built part. Data frozen at FY2026. No data aggregator used. TCPL prints no EBITDA definition in the pages read, so the gap explanation is our arithmetic. No consolidated gross-margin bridge in the report, so the page states none.

inventory.item: A margin = paise kept from each rupee of sales
Gross margin = (sales - materials) / sales; Ramu 50%
EBITDA margin; Ramu 17%
EBIT (operating) margin; Ramu 14.6% (73/500)
Net margin; Ramu 10%
What each margin tells you (product pricing vs input cost, operating business, after wear, after everything)
Variable costs: materials 2.50 + freight 0.25 = 2.75/cup, 275 cr
Fixed costs: staff 60, rent/ads/power 80, depreciation 12 = 152 (cash 140)
Statements list costs by nature, so fixed/variable split is an estimate; real fixed costs creep
inventory.locator: Part 3 + TCPL statement p.415 (lists costs by nature)

inventory.item: Contribution = price - variable cost = 2.25/cup, 45%
Break-even = fixed cash 140 / 2.25 = 62.2 cr cups; EBIT break-even 67.6
Operating leverage: sales +10% -> EBITDA +26%, EBIT +31% (110 cr cups: 247.5-140=107.5; 95.5)
Same leverage works in reverse: -10% -> EBIT -31%; zero at -32% sales
DOL = contribution / EBIT = 225/73 = 3.1; larger near break-even (6.4 at 80, 2.3 at 120)
DOL holds for volume changes; a 10% price rise gives EBIT +68%
High-fixed vs low-fixed cost businesses: Ramu +/-31% vs one-off low-fixed example +/-17%
Financial leverage (debt) is Part 11
Compare margins over years: Ramu net margin 9.1% to 10.0% FY22-FY26; PAT CAGR 13.6% vs sales 11.0%
Peer comparison traps (business model, definition, one-offs); full treatment Part 15
Lab: four sliders, margins, % change vs base, stacked split, +/-10% presets
TCPL gross margin FY26 41.6%, FY25 42.8%
TCPL EBITDA computed 13.8% (2,791.80) vs presented 13.9% (2,815); FY25 14.1% vs 14.2% (2,502)
inventory.locator: statement p.415; MD&A p.223; AGM slide 8

inventory.item: Reason for the gap: other income counted in segment results (164.75-141.76=22.99; FY25 23.08)
TCPL net margin 7.6% (FY25 7.3%)
FY25->FY26 drivers: cost shares, D&A +4.3% vs sales +15.2%, finance costs 290.20->137.03, tax rate 22.3->24.6%

Report-stated reasons: tea/coffee volatility (p.212), H2 FY25 price rises (p.223), coffee price movements (p.222), standalone tapering tea cost inflation (p.224), interest on acquisition borrowings (p.224), FY25 one-time tax credit (p.223), India vs international/non-branded margin (p.223)
Segment result margins India 9.1->11.8, International 14.7->11.9, Non-branded 21.3->11.7
Hand-off to Part 9 (growth)

assumptions: variable cost per cup = materials + freight 0.25; sliders move materials, freight fixed at 0.25
fixed cash costs include staff 60 and rent/ads/power 80 at default
depreciation 12, other income 4, finance costs 10 constant
tax = 17/67 of positive pre-tax profit, none on a loss
gross profit = sales - materials only (freight sits in other expenses)
% changes are against the canonical base (EBITDA 85, EBIT 73, sales 500)
